mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous three months signals strong consumer demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances with positive RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) annualized growth is below 1%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the previous two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for broader economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals an economic contraction, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.
